newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk workers protest over pay arrears.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk workers protest over pay arrears.

text.p: Workers at Russia's Norilsk Nickel combine have passed a vote of no-confidence in management over wage arrears, but metals output is proceeding as planned, a Norilsk spokeswoman said on Monday.

Lyubov Zub, a specialist at the combine's information section, said by telephone from the Arctic town of Norilsk that labour union representatives met managers on Saturday but that no agreements were reached.
She said workers were not preparing to strike but that disruptions could occur if demands were not met by February 20.
"They (the representatives) set certain conditions -- economic conditions -- covering wage arrears as well as the development of investments for production," she said.
She said most workers at the combine, the flagship plant of the Norilsk Nickel metals group, had just been paid for September and some for October.

Production of nickel, copper and cobalt at the combine, known as the Norilsk Mining and Enriching Complex, was going according to plan, and nickel output was slightly above targeted levels, she said. She gave no concrete figures.
She said the plant's technology made it difficult to disrupt or halt output, and that refusing to unload metals for export was the "most effective means" of disrupting operations.
Labour unrest has hit Norilsk in the past, as Uneximbank, the Russian commercial bank with a 38 percent stake in the group, struggles to implement a rescue package for the financially-troubled plant.
Interfax news agency said pay arrears to plant workers were around one trillion roubles.
It said workers would ask the government to change Norilsk's management and revoke Uneximbank's right to manage the 38 percent stake if demands were not met.
The bank won the stake in a shares-for-loans auction last year.
